final_verification.scope: Actual Kafka arrival replay; no live scheduler execution or energy benchmark.

implementation.broker_health: Reused locked Kafka admin client; 10-second observation interval; explicit reconnect bypasses interval
implementation.controller_integration: Validated subprocess argument lists invoking existing controller start --background / stop and explicit verifier
implementation.queries: Read-only coherent SQLite WAL snapshots; 25 sessions/page and 600 observations/chart; no event-table scans per refresh
implementation.refresh: Native fragment: 2 s following an active session, 15 s inspecting history during another active replay, otherwise no automatic poll
implementation.worker_lifecycle: External controller process; no producer or consumer loop in Streamlit

implementation_issue_fixed: Mixed active/completed history converts missing end times to NaN in Pandas. Timestamp formatting now handles missing/nonfinite values and has a regression test.
known_limitations: Three historical research provenance hash references remain unresolved.
Arrival transport is not live scheduling, energy measurement, utilization, allocation or observed SLA outcomes.
Publication throughput history is not recorded; the UI shows actual acknowledged totals rather than an invented series.
Resource-skew composition is the whole verified source population; consumed skew aggregates are not inferred.
Controller acknowledgement totals persist in batches and can temporarily trail consumption.
Broker reachability is an observed check cached up to ten seconds, with its timestamp shown.
Old sessions may have no lag samples or detailed receipt; absence stays explicit until optional verification.
A dead controller requires documented controller/CLI recovery; the UI does not erase history or silently clear active state.
At-least-once transport with idempotent SQLite persistence; single broker, no high availability.
Measured timing/throughput are local transport observations, not scheduler benchmarks.
